results.quote: For a subspace \EuScript{U}\in\mathscr{L}(\mathscr{A}_\mathbb{P}) whose equations involve \kappa pieces, for which \alpha(\EuScript{U};n) has period p, the number of values of \alpha(\EuScript{U};n) that are sufficient to determine all the coefficients in all constituents is \lceil p(\kappa-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{codim}\EuScript{U})\rceil+\varepsilon, where \varepsilon=1 if \mathrm{codim}\EuScript{U} is even and 0 if it is odd.

For a partial nightrider \mathbb{N}^k, the coefficient q!\gamma_i of n^{2q-i} in o_{\mathbb{N}^k}(q;n) is a polynomial in q, periodic in n, with leading term \left[-\frac{5k}{24}\right]^i\frac{q^{2i}}{i!}.

The third coefficient of the partial nightrider counting quasipolynomial is independent of n; it is \gamma_2=\frac{1}{2!(q-2)!}\left\{\left(\frac{5k}{24}\right)^2(q-2)_2+\left(\frac{k}{8}+\frac{11\lambda_1}{32}+\frac{53\lambda_2}{144}+\frac{27\lambda_3}{80}\right)(q-2)+(k-1)\right\}.
The next coefficient, \gamma_3, is periodic in n with period 2 and periodic part (-1)^n\frac{1}{3!(q-2)!}\left\{\frac{3k}{8}\right\}.
The coefficient \gamma_4 has period 2 and periodic part -(-1)^n\frac{1}{4!(q-2)!}\big\{\frac{5k^2}{16}(q-2)_2+\big(\frac{3k}{2}+\frac{9\lambda_2}{4}\big)(q-2)\big\},
